008package paint.shared.utils;
009
010import tech.tablesaw.io.csv.CsvReadOptions;
011
012import java.io.BufferedReader;
013import java.io.IOException;
014import java.io.InputStreamReader;
015import java.io.Reader;
016import java.nio.charset.CharacterCodingException;
017import java.nio.charset.Charset;
018import java.nio.charset.CharsetDecoder;
019import java.nio.charset.CodingErrorAction;
020import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
021import java.nio.file.Files;
022import java.nio.file.Path;
023import java.util.List;
024
025/**
026 * Reads text files (the CSV files of a project) in the right character set.
027 * <p>
028 * The application writes UTF-8. Files edited in Excel on Windows may instead be Windows-1252
029 * ("CSV (Comma delimited)") or UTF-8 preceded by a byte order mark ("CSV UTF-8"). A file is read as
030 * UTF-8 when it is valid UTF-8, otherwise as Windows-1252, which is logged as a warning; a byte
031 * order mark is skipped. Text with characters such as µ, é or ° in Windows-1252 is practically
032 * never valid UTF-8, so the choice is reliable.
033 * <p>
034 * Since Java 18 the default character set is UTF-8 on every system, so without this a
035 * Windows-1252 file would lose those characters silently (or stop the reading with an error).
036 */
037public final class TextFiles {
038
039    /** Character set of files saved by Excel on Windows as "CSV (Comma delimited)". */
040    public static final Charset WINDOWS_1252 = Charset.forName("windows-1252");
041
042    private static final char BYTE_ORDER_MARK = '﻿';
043
044    private TextFiles() {
045        // Prevent instantiation
046    }
047
048    /**
049     * The character set to read the file with: UTF-8 if the file is valid UTF-8, otherwise
050     * Windows-1252 (with a warning in the log). The file is checked in a streaming pass, so
051     * large files are not held in memory.
052     *
053     * @param file the file to check
054     * @return {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8} or {@link #WINDOWS_1252}
055     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be read
056     */
057    public static Charset charsetOf(Path file) throws IOException {
058        CharsetDecoder strictUtf8 = StandardCharsets.UTF_8.newDecoder()
059                                                          .onMalformedInput(CodingErrorAction.REPORT)
060                                                          .onUnmappableCharacter(CodingErrorAction.REPORT);
061        try (Reader r = new InputStreamReader(Files.newInputStream(file), strictUtf8)) {
062            char[] buffer = new char[64 * 1024];
063            while (r.read(buffer) >= 0) {
064                // only checking
065            }
066            return StandardCharsets.UTF_8;
067        } catch (CharacterCodingException e) {
068            PaintLogger.warnf("'%s' is not in UTF-8; it was read as Windows-1252 (as saved by Excel on Windows). "
069                                      + "Check that special characters such as µ, é or ° came through correctly.",
070                              file);
071            return WINDOWS_1252;
072        }
073    }
074
075    /**
076     * Opens the file for reading in the character set of {@link #charsetOf(Path)}, after a byte
077     * order mark if there is one.
078     *
079     * @param file the file to read
080     * @return a reader over the text of the file
081     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be read
082     */
083    public static BufferedReader newReader(Path file) throws IOException {
084        BufferedReader reader = Files.newBufferedReader(file, charsetOf(file));
085        reader.mark(1);
086        if (reader.read() != BYTE_ORDER_MARK) {
087            reader.reset();
088        }
089        return reader;
090    }
091
092    /**
093     * Reads the whole file as text, see {@link #newReader(Path)}.
094     *
095     * @param file the file to read
096     * @return the text of the file
097     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be read
098     */
099    public static String readText(Path file) throws IOException {
100        String text = Files.readString(file, charsetOf(file));
101        return !text.isEmpty() && text.charAt(0) == BYTE_ORDER_MARK ? text.substring(1) : text;
102    }
103
104    /**
105     * Reads the file as lines, see {@link #newReader(Path)}. Like
106     * {@link Files#readAllLines(Path)}, the list can be modified.
107     *
108     * @param file the file to read
109     * @return the lines of the file, without line terminators
110     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be read
111     */
112    public static List<String> readAllLines(Path file) throws IOException {
113        List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(file, charsetOf(file));
114        if (!lines.isEmpty() && !lines.get(0).isEmpty() && lines.get(0).charAt(0) == BYTE_ORDER_MARK) {
115            lines.set(0, lines.get(0).substring(1));
116        }
117        return lines;
118    }
119
120    /**
121     * Tablesaw CSV read options for the file, see {@link #newReader(Path)}. The table is named
122     * after the file, as {@code Table.read().csv(file)} does.
123     *
124     * @param file the CSV file to read
125     * @return a builder to add further options to
126     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be read
127     */
128    public static CsvReadOptions.Builder csvReadOptions(Path file) throws IOException {
129        return CsvReadOptions.builder(newReader(file))
130                             .tableName(file.getFileName().toString());
131    }
132}
